summary: Intro demo of Redwood Console focusing on per-route telemetry, chargeback mapping, and cost breakdown. Customer concerns: mapping internal routes to Redwood routes, SSO & SOC2, demo of per-route cost attribution and a pilot to validate actual token-level spend. Next steps: share security docs, run benchmark, and exchange route mapping CSV for chargeback setup.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: ok everyone, hi thanks for joining, we should be live. this is Maya from Redwood, AE, and Jared my SE is also here. quick roll call?
[00:07] Priya Nair: hey hi, Priya here, head of ML at Cythera. Oskar and Sofia are on as well.
[00:12] Oskar Lund: yep, Oskar, platform. Tom from SRE might pop in later.
[00:16] Sofia Gomez: Sofia, FinOps. excited to see the chargeback bits.
[00:19] Maya Chen: great. agenda today — quick context from you, then console walkthrough focused on telemetry and chargeback maps, then Q&A and next steps.
[00:28] Priya Nair: our problem: we want predictable inference cost across teams. we have 6 product teams using multiple models, some hosted, some self-hosted. we need to attribute spend to teams and routes, and also reduce latency spikes. main asks: per-route cost visibility, mapping to our billing system, SSO + SOC2 compliance.
[00:45] Jared Patel: thanks, that helps. quick note: our console exposes per-route token usage, per-model latency percentiles, cache hit rates, and an export for chargebacks. we'll demo a live tenant with synthetic data — names masked.
[00:58] Maya Chen: share deck link in chat — short security doc link too. (link: https://redwood.app/sec-pack)
[01:05] Oskar Lund: saw that, quick Q — how do you correlate our internal routes (like /api/generate-chat) with Redwood routes? we use internal routing tags and k8s labels.
[01:15] Jared Patel: good question — two approaches. best practice: pass a route header on request (x-rw-route) and attach org tags. second: we can map telemetry server-side by matching metadata (we support mapping rules in the console, regex-based). if not available, we can ingest your us-east-1 LB logs and map by IP ranges.
[01:32] Sofia Gomez: and then we can export a CSV for our finops tool, right?
[01:37] Jared Patel: yes — exports include route, model, tokens in/out, estimated gpu-second cost, and allocation tags. you can also push to S3 or BigQuery.
[01:45] Priya Nair: curious on how you estimate "gpu-second" cost for mixed-precision quantized models — we use int8 and bfloat16 across different services.
[01:52] Jared Patel: the console uses model profiles plus hardware profiles. we have measured throughput curves and a kernel-cost model. for quantized variants we apply a scaling factor; for mixed-workloads we report a blended unit cost. it's an estimate but we've seen <10% variance in practice.
[02:08] Maya Chen: demo time — jumping into Console.
[02:12] [screen share begins]
[02:15] Jared Patel: home page shows tenant overview — tokens, embeddings, active routes. i'm opening the Routes tab.
[02:22] [02:22] Jared Patel: here are routes — left is your routes table, you can pin favorites. note the filter for model family and region. look at route /chat/assistant — you can expand it.
[02:33] [02:33] Oskar Lund: are those timestamps in UTC?
[02:35] Jared Patel: yes, defaults to UTC but you can configure timezone per-user.
[02:40] [03:00] Jared Patel: expanding route — shows 95th latency graph, token breakdown by input/output, and a small panel "Economics" which breaks down estimated cost into: serving (gpu), tokens (license), infra (network), and caching savings.
[03:14] Sofia Gomez: where does the caching savings come from?
[03:16] Jared Patel: from prefix/KV cache hits. Console tracks KV cache hit rates and estimated tokens avoided. we show both absolute tokens saved and estimated $ saved.
[03:25] Priya Nair: ok i'm seeing a big spike 2 days ago in latency — can you show drilldown?
[03:30] Jared Patel: click "drilldown" — this brings up a timeline with traces, per-model tail-latency, and batch sizes. i'm toggling to show requests with large contexts — looks like a small subset of requests with 8k+ context caused long kernel pulls.
[03:47] Oskar Lund: that would line up with a file-upload scenario, yes. is there an alerting rule?
[03:51] Jared Patel: yes, Console has SLOs and alerts per-route; we can auto-trigger a canary to fallback model or throttle. you can also set a fallback route to a lower-cost quantized model automatically.
[04:05] Maya Chen: (interruption) a note on fallbacks — teams often configure a tiered policy: low-latency routes get dedicated pool, bulk/cheap routes go to shared or quantized. reduces unit cost.
[04:16] Priya Nair: can we tag routes to internal cost centers? we want immediate chargeback to product owners.
[04:20] Jared Patel: yes, each route can have metadata tags and a "billing code" field. the export maps tag -> cost center. you can also provide a mapping file and we'll do one-time mapping in Console.
[04:33] Sofia Gomez: when you say export, is it daily or hourly? we need hourly for internal showback dashboards.
[04:38] Jared Patel: hourly exports are available; for higher granularity, we can stream to a webhook or to your data warehouse.
[04:45] [05:00] Jared Patel: toggling to "Cost Explorer" — this is where you can compare routes by cost, tokens, and efficiency. I'm grouping by team tag and showing cost per 1k requests. notice inefficiency metric: tokens per useful token (we try to estimate redundant tokens).
[05:20] Priya Nair: hmm tokens per useful token — is that measured by our eval set or heuristics?
[05:24] Jared Patel: heuristics initially — pattern detection for repetition, no-response, high-generation-to-prompt ratio. for stricter measurement you can upload eval prompts and we'll score against that prompt set.
[05:36] Oskar Lund: you mentioned streaming exports to BigQuery — what's the connector?
[05:40] Jared Patel: we have a native BigQuery sink and S3/Redshift connector. setup is in the Integrations tab — you add a service account and map dataset.
[05:49] Sofia Gomez: security: how are audit logs retained and encrypted? we need customer-managed keys (KMS) and 12 month retention.
[05:56] Maya Chen: Redwood Private supports KMS and HSM integrations, and audit logs can be retained per your policy. hosted tier has default retention 90 days but enterprise plans can extend and use CSEK/KMS. I'll attach the security pack with specifics.
[06:12] [06:30] Priya Nair: great. moving on: pilot specifics — we want a 2-week pilot to run ~5 million tokens/week to validate cost models and latency under our real traffic. what does Redwood need?
[06:42] Jared Patel: we'll request a mapping CSV, a sample request trace, and service account for pushing telemetry. we can provision a dedicated test pool with constrained GPUs to mimic your baseline. we also need a white-listed prefix for test traffic.
[06:54] Oskar Lund: any quota limits? we prefer to ramp.
[06:57] Jared Patel: standard pilot quotas are flexible; we'll size based on expected tokens. usage will be tracked in Console and annotated as "pilot" for billing separation.
[07:06] [07:30] Maya Chen: walk-through of chargeback mapping: inside Route settings, click "Export mapping" — sample CSV has columns route, tag, cost_center, default_model. you can populate and re-upload; Console will apply retroactive attribution for the past 30 days.
[07:48] Sofia Gomez: retroactive attribution is huge for us. will that change invoice numbers?
[07:52] Jared Patel: invoices won't change retroactively for billing, but internal reports and exports will reflect the updated attribution so your internal cost reports align.
[08:01] Priya Nair: question on multi-region routing — our EU traffic must stay in EU for data residency. can you limit models to eu-west-1?
[08:09] Jared Patel: yes, routing policy supports region pinning; you can pin routes to region or set fallback to nearest region. for Private we can deploy control plane in your VPC region.
[08:20] Oskar Lund: how do you handle model variants? for instance we have LLM-X and LLM-X-quant. does the console show conversions between variants?
[08:29] Jared Patel: we show model lineage; you can view variant performance side-by-side and the console suggests quantization where latency/cost tradeoff is acceptable. there's also an Optimize tab that recommends quant profiles per route.
[08:42] Priya Nair: can Optimize recommend batching configs? we see throughput differences across teams.
[08:47] Jared Patel: yes — Optimize simulates batching gains and suggests target batch sizes and concurrency per route given latency SLOs. it also recommends cache TTLs.
[08:59] [09:15] Maya Chen: a quick detour — competitor question: some teams considered Anthropic or building TGI in-house. typical objections: cost of self-hosting vs Redwood's managed plus observability. any comments?
[09:26] Priya Nair: yes we evaluated TGI; it's cheaper compute-wise but we worry about operational burden.
[09:31] Jared Patel: exactly — Redwood aims to reduce ops cost by providing batching, KV caching, and model kernel optimizations. many customers find overall TCO lower when accounting for engineering time.
[09:46] Sofia Gomez: okay show me a sample export for FinOps.
[09:50] [10:00] Jared Patel: exporting now — CSV preview: date,hour,route,model,tokens_in,tokens_out,est_gpu_sec, est_cost_usd, tag, cost_center. here's a sample line: 2026-05-12,12,/chat/assistant,redwood-3b,420,890,0.004,0.021,prod-chat,team-alpha.
[10:23] Priya Nair: that est_gpu_sec number — is it per request or aggregated?
[10:27] Jared Patel: per-row estimate, aggregated in exports. you can change granularity (minute/hour/day).
[10:34] Oskar Lund: small nit — we have internal request IDs. can we include a correlation id in the export?
[10:38] Jared Patel: yes add x-rw-cid and we'll include it as a column if forwarded.
[10:44] [11:00] Priya Nair: SSO question — we use Okta. support for SAML? we need RBAC enforced.
[11:05] Maya Chen: yes, SAML/Okta supported, SCIM for user provisioning, and RBAC per-route. for Private deploy we can also enable VPC peering.
[11:16] Tom Rhee (joined): hey sorry late, quick question on KV cache: is cache shared across customers in hosted?
[11:22] Jared Patel: hosted cache is per-tenant logically separated; for Dedicated you can have isolated caches on pool. nothing is shared across customers.
[11:32] Tom Rhee: thanks.
[11:34] [12:00] Jared Patel: moving to "Alerts & Playbooks" — you can attach an automated rollback if latency > X for Y minutes. in the playbook we can failover to a fallback model or reduce max_context.
[12:15] Priya Nair: fallback behavior needs to preserve semantics; does fallback rewrite prompts?
[12:19] Jared Patel: no automatic rewrite, but you can define response templates or suffix prompts for lower-tier models. also function-calling remains consistent.
[12:30] Sofia Gomez: about chargeback accuracy — what error margin should we expect between Console estimates and actual cloud bill?
[12:37] Jared Patel: for served tokens and GPU-time our median error historically is ~6–9% during pilots; depends on model variance and quantization fidelity. that's why we recommend pilot runs.
[12:49] [13:00] Maya Chen: ok quick recap of benefits: per-route cost breakdown, mapping to cost centers, hourly export/streaming, automated fallbacks, and an Optimize module for batching/quantization.
[13:12] Priya Nair: good. any prerequisites for pilot?
[13:16] Jared Patel: sample traces, mapping CSV, and a service account. also decide which routes to include — suggest start with 3 high-volume routes.
[13:25] Oskar Lund: we'll prepare mapping and sample traces by Mon.
[13:29] Sofia Gomez: will you include an estimate sheet for pilot pricing?
[13:32] Maya Chen: yes, I'll send pilot pricing and a template for expected usage.
[13:36] [14:00] Priya Nair: one more question on privacy — does Redwood keep prompt payloads for troubleshooting? we need data masking.
[14:07] Jared Patel: we can mask PII on ingest and redact in payload retention settings. default retention is 30 days for payloads; logs non-payload can be kept per enterprise settings.
[14:19] Tom Rhee: do you support audit logs to our SIEM?
[14:22] Jared Patel: yes, we can stream audit logs to your SIEM via syslog or Kinesis.
[14:30] [15:00] Maya Chen: ok let's capture next steps — we'll send security pack, you send mapping and sample traces; Jared will setup the pilot cluster once mapping received.
[15:12] Priya Nair: sounds good. thanks, useful session.
[15:16] Oskar Lund: thanks, appreciate the demo.
[15:19] Sofia Gomez: thanks.
[15:21] Maya Chen: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invite for 5/25.
[15:25] [call ends]
